subject: Scaling efficiency pilot — credits, packaging, and quant roadmap
messages:
From: Claire O'Neill <claire@edgegrid.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeGrid Procurement <procurement@edgegrid.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T13:08:00Z
Subject: Inquiry — efficiency pilot & quantization guidance

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the run-through on Tuesday. We're finalizing internal budgeting for a scaled chat use case and need a short checklist for commercial and technical items to sign off a 3-month Efficiency Pilot with Redwood. High level: 10M tokens/month baseline, 99th percentile latency target ~120ms, and a non-negotiable privacy clause for a subset of PII flows.

Specifically, could you confirm:
- Recommended quantization profile for production (FP16 vs 4-bit) for the Titan-Like model you suggested?
- How prefix/KV caching would be priced — is it token-discounted or included in credits?
- Short list of packaging options that would preserve latency SLO while giving us at least 20% unit-cost improvement vs open GPU self-hosting.

I'm attaching a short workload sample and our draft SOW (EdgeGrid_SOW_Draft.pdf, optimizer_workload_sample.json).

Also looping Tom from ops and procurement. Would appreciate a one-page commercial sketch we can show execs.

Best,
Claire O'Neill
Head of Platform
EdgeGrid

--- Attachment stubs: EdgeGrid_SOW_Draft.pdf (pdf), optimizer_workload_sample.json (json)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Neill <claire@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T17:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry — efficiency pilot & quantization guidance

Claire — great to connect. Quick summary below; I penciled in numbers so you have something for the exec deck. If this looks directionally right we can turn it into a 1-page agreement and a precise quote.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Quantization: start with PTQ 4-bit (QN4) for non-PII routes; use FP16 for PII-tagged requests for safety and higher fidelity. We can serve both variants and route automatically with minimal overhead. Expect ~2.5-3x Token-$ saving on QN4 vs FP16 on average for generation workloads.
- Caching: KV/prefix caching is included as an optimization layer; cost model is credits consumed per output token but we apply an internal effective discount when cache hit rate > 40%. For pilot pricing we offer a 25% effective credit uplift applied to baseline tokens to account for model variants and fallbacks.
- Packaging options:
  1) Pilot (3mo) — Reserved baseline of 10M tokens/month, 30% discounted credits, dedicated GPU pool slices for predictable 99th P99 latency-targeting.
  2) Hybrid Commit — Month-to-month baseline with commit bands (10M / 25M / 50M) and dynamic autoscale; higher discounts at band thresholds, quantization advisory included.
  3) Enterprise Private — Private VPC deployment + on-prem option for PII lanes; separate fee + support SLA.

Commercial sketch (pilot):
- Term: 3 months
- Baseline: 10,000,000 tokens/month
- Pilot credit rate: 0.0009 USD/credit (example) with 30% credit discount applied to baseline (net effective rate ~0.00063/token)
- One-time onboarding fee: $12,000 (includes quant tuning + ops runbook)
- Success milestone: if cache hit > 45% and average latency <120ms, 2-month extension credit at 15% off list.

Ops notes / security:
- For PII-tagged requests we recommend a dedicated FP16 variant and KMS-backed keying. SOC2 artifacts available (we'll share).
- We'll provide a short quant-quality checklist (WER/ROUGE-style checks + hallucination spot checks) as part of onboarding.

Next steps: I'll route an internal Ops/Eng call (Sofia + Karthik) to review the workload sample and produce an SLO/arch note. Is Friday 10am PT good for you?

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com

--- Attachment referenced: pricing_workbook.xlsx (estimate workbook)

From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@edgegrid.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Claire O'Neill <claire@edgegrid.ai>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:16:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry — efficiency pilot & quantization guidance

Rafael / Claire — thanks. A few clarifying questions from our ops/procurement side: 
1) On the 25% effective uplift for pilot — can you convert that into an explicit monthly fee or credit bucket we can sign to? Procurement prefers fixed commitments for the pilot.
2) If we run the FP16 PII lane in Private mode, how are license/support costs split vs hosted?
3) Can you confirm whether the 30% discount you quoted is stackable with volume-tier discounts, or is it the pilot-only discount?

Also attached is our procurement rubric — we typically need a minimal SLA and a two-week termination notice for pilots. Happy to take the 10am PT call Friday; we'll add our legal lead if needed.

Thanks,
Tom Lee
Head of Ops, EdgeGrid

--- Attachment stubs: procurement_rubric.pdf

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@edgegrid.ai>, Claire O'Neill <claire@edgegrid.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T18:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Inquiry — efficiency pilot & quantization guidance

Tom — answers inline and next steps.

1) Pilot uplift / fixed bucket: we can do a fixed credit bucket model. For the 10M token baseline I propose a 12M-credit bucket for the 3-month pilot priced at $22,680 (reflects the 25% uplift for variant/fallback overhead). That converts the uplift into a single invoiceable line item.

2) FP16 PII lane in Private mode: Private deployment carries a platform seat + managed infra surcharge. For pilots we can offer a discounted Private add-on of $6k/mo (instead of the standard $12k) for the 3-month term; support/patching included. Long-term licensing will follow the Enterprise Private T&Cs.

3) Stacking discounts: pilot discount (30% off baseline credit rate) is stackable with volume-tier discounts; we cap stackable discounts at 45% total on the baseline. Any overage tokens beyond the bucket are billed at list rates with standard volume tiers.

Legal / SLA: 2-week termination for pilots is fine. We'll add a P99 latency objective and an escalation path in the SOW; breaches trigger a credit remediation ladder. I'll attach SOC2 and a short SLO draft ahead of Friday.

Action items:
- Sofia & Karthik to run the workload sample and return a short latency/quantization runbook by Thursday COB.
- Rafael to generate 1-page commercial sketch + DocuSign-ready SOW (will include the 12M credit bucket line and Private add-on).
- Schedule: Friday 10am PT ops+procurement sync.

Thanks — Rafael
